title: A Router by Hand
learning_objectives: Match request paths against patterns with path parameters
Return 404, 405 (with Allow) and 422 at the right times
entry_point: class Router; Router.route(method, pattern); Router.dispatch(method, path, query=None)
hints: Write `_match(segments, parts)` returning a dict of raw params or None: lengths equal, literal segments equal, `{...}` segments captured.
First collect every route whose pattern matches the path; none → 404; none with this method → 405 with `", ".join(sorted(methods))`.
For `{name:int}`, `int(raw)` inside try/except ValueError → 422; the handler result is a dict or a `(status, dict)` tuple.

failure_feedback.advice: Convert `{item_id:int}` with int() and pass `query=` to the handler.
A path matches only when it has the same number of segments and equal literals.
If the path matches but the method does not, return 405 with the sorted allowed methods.
Catch the int() conversion error and return 422 with loc ['path', name].
Try routes in registration order and compare methods in upper case.
The decorator must register the function and return it unchanged.
